newsitem.title: USA: Planning Sciences sees "small" Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Planning Sciences sees "small" Q1 profit.

text.p: Planning Sciences International Plc Wednesday said it expects to make a "small" profit for the first quarter ended March 31.

The company also said it expects revenues for the first quarter to be between $6.7 and $7.2 million, as compared to $5.2 million for the same quarter last year. Final results for the quarter will be released prior to the market opening on May 1.

Paul Rolph, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said "this quarter's results have been disappointing ... several large potential orders were not booked in the United Kingdom in the quarter." Rolph added that the company continues to pursue these orders, although no assurances can be given that they will be booked.
Rolph said, however, that the company is pleased with the progress made this quarter in the U.S. and that the company will continue to devote significant time to developing its U.S. business.
Planning Sciences supplies network-centric software for enterprise planning and decision making.
